<reason>A won by pinning the motion on its only novel clause—apps “cannot easily bypass”—and forcing a live fork: either a voluntary flag (the suggestion-regime B had already called “no rule”) or attesting, locked-down architecture. B’s household-account middle path never closed borrowed-login, browser, or vendor-as-regulator holes, and Rebuttal 2 being clipped left that pressure under-answered. B’s responsibility-versus-the-feed frame was real but did not neutralize A’s comparative weighing of existing tools versus cage costs.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s first rebuttal isolating that everything B defends already exists, so the whole cost sits in bypass-proofing, then locking B into the suggestion-versus-cage fork on servers, browsers, and later borrowed logins.</best_rebuttal>
